write.prompt: Some people think that life skills should be taught in one short lesson every week, while others believe it is better to hold a few full days of hands-on practice during the school year. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
mustUse: hai mẫu tường thuật khác nhau
một câu chuyển sang đánh giá
ý riêng xuất hiện ở cả thesis và kết bài
write.modelAfterSubmit:
Most schools agree that students need practical life skills, but they disagree about how to fit them into the timetable. Some people prefer a short lesson every week, whereas others argue that a few full days of hands-on practice are more effective. In my view, a combination of the two would work best.

Supporters of weekly lessons point out that skills are learnt through regular practice. A student who plans a simple budget every week is more likely to remember the steps than one who tries it only once a term. Short lessons also fit easily into the timetable and are less tiring, so students are unlikely to lose interest.

On the other hand, it is often argued that some skills cannot be learnt in forty minutes. Cooking a full meal or practising first aid on a dummy takes time to set up, and a short lesson may end just as students start to understand. A full practice day allows them to repeat each task several times with trained staff. While both views are reasonable, the second seems more convincing for complex skills.

In conclusion, I believe schools should hold a hands-on practice day each term for demanding skills such as first aid, and then use short weekly lessons to help students remember what they have learnt.
